facts.label: Site-wide consumption far below the period norm
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. Same robust outlier test as the fuel spike rule, applied to site-wide monthly consumption. Explicitly NOT corrected: the incident register records a regional substation failure and three weeks on backup generation for the month this fires, so the reading is real. A pipeline that "smoothed" it would erase the most important event in the period.

facts.label: Gap in the meter numbering
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. Meters run MTR-01 to MTR-07 with MTR-06 absent for all 18 months. Either it was decommissioned, or a load is not being reported. Nothing in the export says which, and the difference matters: one is fine, the other is missing Scope 2. Flagged as a question for the client rather than assumed away.

facts.label: Meter readings recorded in MWh but labelled kWh
facts.detail: 9 finding(s), severity error, action fixed. MTR-07 reads ~250,000 kWh a month through September 2025, then ~250 from October onward, with the unit column still saying kWh. A ventilation and dewatering load does not fall by 99.9% and stay there for nine months. Detected by order of magnitude within each meter, not by hard-coding the meter and date, and corrected x1000 with the factor recorded per row. This is the single largest error in the dataset: uncorrected it understates Scope 2 for half the reporting period.

facts.label: Negative quantity — appears to be a credit note
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. INV-41777 records -12,500 L against -$23,375.00, and its invoice number sits outside the 40xxx block used by every other row. That reads as a credit note — fuel invoiced then reversed — not as corruption. It is loaded with is_credit_note=true so it nets off the totals, because deleting it would overstate consumption while "correcting" the sign would double-count it. Flagged for the client to confirm.

facts.label: Delivery date states month only
facts.detail: 29 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. Dates like `Oct-25` have no day. The row is anchored to the first of the month and marked date_precision=month. Monthly emissions stay correct; anything day-level must exclude these, and can now tell which they are. Inventing a plausible day would make an unknown look like a fact.

facts.label: Duplicate invoice number
facts.detail: 7 finding(s), severity error, action rejected. Seven invoice numbers appear twice, each time as an exact repeat of every other field. Two identical deliveries on the same invoice is not a thing that happens, so the second copy is a re-export artefact. The first is kept, the copy is rejected and recorded here with a pointer to the survivor. Counting both would inflate Scope 1 by roughly half a million litres.

facts.label: Mixed date and currency formats within a column
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action fixed. One column carries three date formats (ISO, day-first slash, month-year) and costs appear both as "$182,946.64" and as 132182.58. Normalised on read. Reported once for the file rather than on every row: it is systematic, and 150 identical findings would bury the rare ones.

facts.label: Column headers carry stray whitespace
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action fixed. Headers are written as `Invoice No`, ` Delivery Date`, `Fuel Type `, ` Unit`. Trimmed on read. Cosmetic, but recorded because it is a reliable sign the file was assembled by hand rather than exported, which is context for how much else to trust.

facts.label: No fuel deliveries recorded for a month inside the reporting period
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity error, action flagged. November 2025 contains no fuel invoices at all, between an October with 8 and a December with 7. The site was plainly operating — the meters record a full month of electricity — so this is missing paperwork, not a shutdown. Scope 1 is understated for that month by roughly a month of diesel, and nothing else in the file draws attention to it: a gap is invisible unless you go looking for the absence of rows. Flagged rather than interpolated. Estimating the missing volume would put an invented number into a compliance report.

facts.label: Bulk diesel delivered to a light-vehicle fleet
facts.detail: 3 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. The Light Vehicles fleet otherwise takes petrol in consistent ~4,000 L loads. A few tens of thousands of litres of diesel against that site area is most likely a coding error at the invoice level. Flagged, not reassigned: we do not know which area it belongs to, and moving fuel between areas on a guess would produce a confident, wrong site breakdown.

facts.label: Quantity recorded in kilolitres
facts.detail: 11 finding(s), severity error, action fixed. Eleven rows record kL against a column whose other 139 rows are litres. Converted x1000, with the original value and unit retained. Confirmed independently by cost: after conversion these rows imply $1.73-$1.93/L, inside the range set by every other delivery; before conversion they imply roughly $1,800/L. Left uncorrected this understates Scope 1 by about 750,000 litres — an error in the direction nobody questions.

facts.label: Monthly fuel volume far above the period norm
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action flagged. Outliers are found with a modified z-score against the median absolute deviation, not a hand-picked multiple of the median. A fixed multiple has to be tuned against the answer you already expect, and would have missed this dataset: the one anomalous month is 1.49x the median, under any round threshold you would have chosen in advance, while sitting about eight deviations clear of a series that otherwise holds between 0.85x and 1.14x. Not a defect — the pipeline noticing something real. Read with ELEC-CONSUMPTION-DROP-01 for the same month.

facts.label: Identical description reused across incidents
facts.detail: 9 finding(s), severity info, action flagged. Several descriptions appear word for word on multiple incidents at different dates and locations. Two very different explanations: copy-paste in the register, or a hazard genuinely recurring without being addressed. Flagged rather than deduplicated, because the second reading is a finding in its own right — one description here repeats five times across four locations.

facts.label: Incident ID used for more than one incident
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity error, action fixed. INC-2025-011 identifies two different incidents on two different dates with different descriptions. Unlike the fuel duplicates these are distinct events, so neither can be dropped. The later row is given a suffixed surrogate key and the register ID is preserved unchanged in source_incident_id, so a client searching their own system still finds it.

facts.label: Incident ID far outside the main sequence
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action flagged. Most IDs form a dense run from 001. A handful sit far above it with a large gap in between, which suggests they were merged in from a different register rather than issued by this one. Worth surfacing on its own terms: these records also turn out to be the ones whose severity does not match their description.

facts.label: Description names a place inconsistent with the recorded location
facts.detail: 3 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. Deliberately narrow: fires only when the text names fixed infrastructure (crusher, wash plant, CHPP, ROM pad, thickener) while the location column holds a mobile fleet. A dust exceedance at the crusher cannot have happened "at" the Haul Fleet. Not corrected — the location column and the description disagree, and the export gives no way to tell which one the client trusts.

facts.label: Text severity mapped to the numeric scale
facts.detail: 11 finding(s), severity info, action fixed. Row-level trace of each Low/Medium value converted to a number, so the mapping is visible per record rather than only as a policy statement.

facts.label: Two severity scales in one column
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. The column mixes Low/Medium with 1/2/3. We map Low=1, Medium=2, High=3, which assumes both are the same three-point scale written differently. That assumption is worth stating rather than burying: many mining registers number severity the other way, with 1 as most severe. If that is the case here, every numeric row is inverted. The AI layer tests the assumption by reading the descriptions.

facts.label: All ABNs fail the ATO checksum
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action flagged. Twelve of the fifteen suppliers carry a correctly formed 11-digit ABN, and all twelve fail the modulus-89 checksum. When a rule fails for 100% of the rows it applies to, the honest conclusion is that the source is systematically different from what the rule assumes — synthetic or masked values — not that the client has twelve separate problems. Reported once at file level so it does not bury the one genuinely malformed ABN, and no supplier is marked invalid on this basis alone.

facts.label: ABN missing or not 11 digits
facts.detail: 3 finding(s), severity warning, action flagged. An ABN is 11 digits. One supplier records 7, two record none. Flagged, never defaulted to zero or guessed: an ABN is how an entity is identified for tax and procurement, and a wrong one is worse than an absent one.

facts.label: Inconsistent category label
facts.detail: 1 finding(s), severity info, action fixed. The same category is written two ways ("Fuel supply" and "Fuel"). Aligned to the label used by the primary record of the pair, so spend groups correctly.

facts.label: Supplier appears more than once
facts.detail: 2 finding(s), severity error, action fixed. Two entities are listed twice: once as a legal-suffix variant (Pty Ltd / P-L) and once as a spelling error sharing an ABN (Maintenance / Maintanence). Both rows are kept and the duplicate points at its primary, rather than being merged away — the client ledger contains both, and reconciling against it later needs both visible. Unmerged, Ironline reads as $8.94M against a true $10.15M, which is the difference between their largest supplier and their second largest.

claims.text: For January 2025 to June 2026, reported Scope 1 plus Scope 2 emissions were 46929.8 t CO2e, but that position rests on 20 corrected activity records and November 2025 has no fuel invoices, with Scope 1 understated for that month.

Across 18 months, total emissions were 46929.8 t CO2e, made up of Scope 1 emissions of 22052.5 t CO2e and Scope 2 emissions of 24877.4 t CO2e; Scope 1 was 47 % of the period total. The period totals include 20 corrected activity records, so the reported split is correction-dependent.

FY2025 emissions were 15614.6 t CO2e for 6 months of data and are an incomplete financial year, while FY2026 emissions were 31315.2 t CO2e for 12 months of data and are a complete financial year. The pack states the FY2025 figure is not comparable with a full one.

May 2026 was the highest-emitting month at 2879.1 t CO2e, while November 2025 was the lowest-emitting month at 1445.5 t CO2e. November 2025 recorded Scope 1 at 0 t CO2e, Scope 2 at 1445.5 t CO2e, 6 contributing records and 1 corrected record, and the fuel file has no invoices for that month.

March 2026 was the outage month: total emissions were 2401 t CO2e, with Scope 1 at 1893.9 t CO2e, Scope 2 at 507.1 t CO2e and Scope 1 share at 78.9 %. Against the median month, grid consumption was -64.5 %, fuel volume was 51.5 %, Scope 1 was 51.6 %, Scope 2 was -64.5 % and total emissions were -10.3 %, with the incident register recording a regional substation failure and backup diesel generators running for approximately three weeks.
For March 2026, the normal-supply comparison was 2677 t CO2e, while reported total emissions were 2401 t CO2e. The pack states this is a comparison against normal supply, not a forecast.

The register contains 42 incidents for the period: 25 at normalised severity 1, 15 at normalised severity 2 and 2 at normalised severity 3. The AI layer classified 42 incident descriptions and found 14 incidents where the description does not support the recorded severity.

Vehicle & mobile equipment was the largest coded incident group at 13 incidents, followed by Equipment & plant at 8, Environmental at 7, Dust & air quality at 6, Other / uncategorised at 4, Slip, trip & fall at 3 and Electrical & power at 1.

The AI layer identified 4 psychosocial hazards: INC-2025-127, INC-2025-152, INC-2026-109 and INC-2026-134. INC-2025-127 and INC-2026-109 were recorded at severity 1 but assessed from the text as 3, and INC-2026-134 links fatigue to extended shifts covering generator operations and manual restarts during the March power outage.

Two severity mismatches understate higher-consequence descriptions: INC-2025-118 was recorded at severity 1 but assessed from the text as 3 after a fractured forearm and surgery, and INC-2025-141 was recorded at severity 1 but assessed from the text as 3 with an LTI recorded.

Severity overstatement also appears in the AI findings: INC-2025-008 was recorded at severity 3 but assessed from the text as 2, and INC-2026-131 was recorded at severity 3 but assessed from the text as 2 while also explaining the outage month.
The source files generated 99 data-quality findings across 22 rules: 31 findings at severity error, 42 at warning and 26 at info. The recorded actions were 37 fixed, 55 flagged and 7 rejected.

The emissions totals rest on corrected source values: ELEC-UNIT-SCALE-01 fixed 9 MTR-07 readings by x1000, FUEL-UNIT-KL-01 fixed 11 quantity rows by x1000, and the monthly emissions totals include 20 corrected activity records.

Rejected or repaired duplication affects the audit trail: FUEL-DUP-01 rejected 7 exact duplicate invoice copies, INC-DUP-ID-01 fixed 1 incident ID used for more than one incident by adding a suffixed surrogate key, and SUP-DUP-01 fixed 2 supplier duplicate findings while keeping ledger rows visible.

Several material items remain flagged for a human rather than corrected: MTR-06 is absent for all 18 months, November 2025 has no fuel invoices, INV-41777 is loaded as a -12,500 L and -$23,375.00 credit note, and 29 fuel delivery dates state month only.

Scope 3 is not calculable from this export even though the supplier file reports 13 suppliers and 30399000 AUD of spend, because the provided emission factors are activity-based and there is no spend-based factor.
Emissions intensity is not calculable from this export because there is no production data, including no tonnes moved and no operating hours, so there is no denominator.

November 2025 remains a report-changing gap: the monthly total is 1445.5 t CO2e with Scope 1 at 0 t CO2e, and FUEL-MONTH-GAP-01 says Scope 1 is understated for that month because no fuel invoices were recorded.

The fuel activity reconciliation is unresolved: the activity summary reports diesel delivered at 0 litres and petrol delivered at 0 litres, while 143 fuel delivery invoices were loaded and Scope 1 emissions for the period are 22052.5 t CO2e from fuel combustion.
MTR-06 is absent for all 18 months; the pack states this is either a decommissioned meter or an unreported load, and the latter would mean missing Scope 2.

rejected.text: The March 2026 outage counterfactual is 2677 t CO2e compared with the reported total of 2401 t CO2e, and the pack identifies it as a comparison against normal supply rather than a forecast.
rejected.detail: States 2, 2, which do not appear in the cited facts.
